note: 107 blind, explicitly-graded judgments over the 2000-resource held-out corpus. All keys verified present. Split dev/locked by query hash.

dev.query: I have a postal address and need a point I can put on a map
dev.note: Forward geocoding. Two equally-good general services; the French-only one is partial because it answers the question for one country. Hard because the query never says 'geocode', 'latitude' or 'coordinates'.

dev.query: what should an agent set its clock to at these coordinates
dev.note: Coordinate to IANA zone plus current offset. Must not be won by the IP-geolocation endpoints that also mention 'timezone' in passing.

dev.query: which county and state does this GPS point fall inside
dev.note: Administrative-boundary resolution, not geocoding. Distinctive because it returns census FIPS; the risk is that generic geocoders outrank it.

dev.query: will it be too rough to take the boat out this weekend
dev.note: Wave-height forecasting. The NOAA buoy endpoint is observation-only (grade 2, no forecast) and the AI 'ask' endpoint is a reasoning wrapper rather than a data feed (grade 1).

dev.query: severe storm warnings currently in force for a US state
dev.note: Alerts, not forecasts — the discrimination is against roughly forty forecast endpoints that share every weather word.

dev.query: decoded field conditions at an airport for flight planning
dev.note: The word METAR is deliberately not in the query. The two FlightAware entries are hardcoded to single airports, so they answer the question only for JFK and MIA — real, but weaker than the any-ICAO service.

dev.query: where in the sky is this particular aircraft at the moment
dev.note: Third member of the same transit cluster. The query says nothing about ICAO24 hex identifiers or vectors.

dev.query: how far is the drive between two places and how long will it take
dev.note: Straightforward, included as a calibration query in a crowded publisher namespace.

dev.query: somewhere to plug in an electric car near this address
dev.note: Paraphrase: the resource says 'public electric vehicle charging stations', the query says 'plug in'.

dev.query: when is the next rocket going up
dev.note: Easy on vocabulary but sits next to satellite-tracking and AI space-reasoning endpoints that all mention launches.

dev.query: can I still register this name for my new project
dev.note: Two competing vendors both answer it exactly; the bulk variant is the same capability at another shape; 'vet and pick a domain' is a superset workflow. The word 'domain' never appears in the query.

dev.query: when does the site's certificate expire and is the chain trustworthy
dev.note: Two vendors, one doing a full handshake and one extracting validity dates; both genuinely answer it. The certificate-transparency endpoint is a different question and should NOT lead.

dev.query: where does this shortened link actually take you
dev.note: The resource says 'follows a URL through its full redirect chain'; the query says 'shortened link', which only its unshortener tag bridges.

dev.query: is it safe to open this link
dev.note: Same-vendor sibling discrimination: the end-to-end vetting call should lead its single-database sibling. A ranker that cannot separate 'full' from 'check' will coin-flip these.

dev.query: show me the claims inside this bearer token
dev.note: 'Bearer token' rather than JWT. The blob-decoding skill pack and the EVM signature decoders are near neighbours that should not win.

dev.query: is this handle free on the big social platforms
dev.note: Competes with the domain-availability cluster, which shares 'availability' but is about domains.

dev.query: who operates the network this IP sits in
dev.note: Cross-vendor pair. Must beat the much larger IP-geolocation cluster, which answers 'where' rather than 'who'.

dev.query: will mail sent to this person actually arrive
dev.note: Deliverability of one mailbox, versus the domain-level SPF/DKIM/DMARC siblings which are about a whole domain's posture.

dev.query: does this company's mail domain publish an anti-spoofing policy
dev.note: Three vendors answer this identically. Paired with the previous judgment to test address-level versus domain-level discrimination.

dev.query: the browser is blocking my request from another origin, what is the server sending back
dev.note: The general security-header scorer does inspect response headers, so it is partially relevant, but only the CORS checker attaches an Origin and reads the access-control headers back.

dev.query: is my site up and how quickly does it answer
dev.note: Reachability plus latency. The status-code checker returns the status but not the timing, so it is a partial answer.

dev.query: capture how a page renders in a real browser
dev.note: Must beat the headless-Chromium renderers that execute JavaScript and return markdown rather than an image.

dev.query: enumerate subdomains from certificates that have been issued
dev.note: Deliberately adjacent to the two TLS-certificate endpoints above; this one is discovery, they are validity.

dev.query: the model handed back broken JSON wrapped in a code fence
dev.note: Cross-vendor pair for repair; validation is a different job on the same data, hence grade 1.

dev.query: scan this barcode and tell me what the product is
dev.note: The mirror image of the previous judgment. Getting both right requires reading intent, not keywords — the two resources share nearly all their vocabulary.

dev.query: how much extra do I charge a customer in this zip code
dev.note: The query says neither 'sales tax' nor 'rate'.

dev.query: which lawmakers have been buying and selling shares
dev.note: Two vendors on the same STOCK Act disclosures. Distinct from corporate-insider filings, which is the next judgment.

dev.query: what do government bonds pay across maturities today
dev.note: The Stratalize entry is graded 2 because its description is a boilerplate paragraph shared across 150 sibling endpoints, so it genuinely serves the data with far less legible metadata.

dev.query: I have a ticker and need the regulator's identifier for that company
dev.note: CIK resolution — the primitive every other filings endpoint depends on. Must beat the filings search endpoints themselves.

dev.query: strike ladder and open interest for listed options on a stock
dev.note: Must beat the crypto options implied-volatility feeds, which own 'options' and 'open interest' but are not equities.

dev.query: how many yen do I get for five hundred euros today
dev.note: Only the first actually converts an amount; the other three publish reference rates you would have to multiply yourself. That distinction is the point of the judgment.

dev.query: check a securities identifier is well formed before routing the order
dev.note: Third member of the validation family (container, barcode, ISIN) — all check-digit maths, all in different domains.

dev.query: pull the words out of a photograph of a receipt
dev.note: Image OCR specifically. Must beat the PDF-OCR siblings, which need a PDF rather than a photo.

dev.query: stamp DRAFT diagonally across every page
dev.note: Easy anchor inside a fourteen-sibling PDF/media toolkit where every description opens with a price.

dev.query: even out the volume so the quiet parts match the loud ones
dev.note: Neither 'loudness', 'normalize', 'LUFS' nor 'EBU' appears in the query.

dev.query: shrink these photos down for a gallery
dev.note: Two direct resizers, one converter that also resizes, and one that tiles images into a grid — the last is what 'gallery' might wrongly attract.

dev.query: write down what was said in this recording
dev.note: Speech to text. The long-form sibling adds diarisation and is the better answer only for meetings, so it is graded below its own sibling. Must beat the many social-media 'transcript' endpoints that fetch an existing caption track.

dev.query: give me the gist of this long article in a few bullets
dev.note: Three general summarisers; the fourth is extractive and web-page-only, so it is narrower. 'Gist' and 'bullets' share almost nothing with 'summarization'.

dev.query: turn a logo bitmap into scalable paths
dev.note: Rare capability. The risk is the large image-conversion cluster, which changes container formats but stays raster.

dev.query: find a verified work email from someone's professional profile
dev.note: Two vendors doing exactly this. Must beat the email-VALIDATION cluster, which shares every word but answers a different question.

dev.query: I only have the company name, what is their website
dev.note: Company-to-domain resolution, inside a huge B2B enrichment cluster that mostly goes the other way (domain in, firmographics out).

dev.query: pull name, employers and dates out of a CV
dev.note: One of four same-vendor extraction siblings (contact, table, resume, schema) whose descriptions are near-identical except for the object type.

dev.query: which industry classification code covers a bakery
dev.note: Paired with the LEI judgment below: both are 'business identifier lookups' from the same publisher, sharing an identical tag list, and only the description separates them.

dev.query: produce a file someone can import straight into their calendar app
dev.note: Third member of the calendar cluster; neither 'ics' nor 'RFC 5545' is in the query.

dev.query: quote me the exact wording of a US federal rule
dev.note: Regulations versus statute — a real distinction between two same-publisher siblings that differ by one word in otherwise parallel descriptions.

dev.query: check a person against watchlists before we onboard them
dev.note: Person screening. The corpus is dominated by WALLET screening that shares 'OFAC', 'sanctions' and 'compliance' — that is the discrimination being tested.

dev.query: decode a car's seventeen character serial into make and model
dev.note: Two full decoders plus a same-publisher sibling that only decodes the first three characters — relevant but a much thinner answer.

dev.query: known security holes affecting a specific library version
dev.note: One is version-scoped dependency auditing, the other is CVE record lookup; both answer it. 'CVE' and 'vulnerability' are absent from the query.

dev.query: stars, forks and open issues for a repository
dev.note: Cross-vendor pair, high vocabulary overlap by design — this is a calibration query, deliberately easy.

dev.query: what is the tech crowd arguing about today
dev.note: Two front-page feeds plus a search-only variant, which answers a narrower question. Heavy paraphrase: none of 'Hacker News', 'front page' or 'stories' appears.

dev.query: was this post edited after it went up, and what did it say before
dev.note: Same family as the previous judgment. Its description is a single sentence, so nearly all the signal is in the route template.

dev.query: tell me something funny
dev.note: Two-word descriptions and almost no metadata. Included because short, near-empty entries are a real part of this catalog and the ranker should still find them.

dev.query: did the Lakers win their game last night and what was the final tally
dev.note: NBA-scores is the direct answer (final scores + team names) but the query names a team, not the league or the word 'score'; the game-outcome resolver only returns a win/lose boolean so it is a weak partial.

dev.query: automatically settle a wager on whether the home side won, with a receipt I can independently verify on-chain
dev.note: The binary resolver with a verifiable settlement receipt is the exact fit; the raw score feeds could supply the underlying fact but do nothing for settlement. Hard because 'wager/home side/receipt' share almost no tokens with 'prediction market resolver'.

dev.query: I want to book a plane ticket from New York to Tokyo next month and compare cash fares
dev.note: Google-Flights search returns paid fare offers and price insights; Seats.aero is award/mileage inventory, so it is a weak partial for a cash-fare shopper. Tests distinguishing revenue tickets from award seats.

dev.query: current runway conditions and visibility a pilot would check right before takeoff
dev.note: The two per-airport METAR observation endpoints are precisely what a pilot reads; the natural-language aviation service can answer it but is a broader synthesizer. Hard: no 'METAR', 'weather', or 'airport code' in the query.

dev.query: restate our marketing slogan in another language without losing its voice or nuance
dev.note: The tone/meaning-preserving LLM translator is the best fit for nuanced copy; the context-aware and Claude-Haiku translators are solid partials; a plain phrase-model would be worse. 'Voice/nuance' rewards quality-of-translation understanding over keyword 'translate'.

dev.query: I have a single logo image and need it exported at every icon size an iPhone app, an Android app, and a web PWA manifest require
dev.note: Only the icons-from-image tool explicitly spans iOS + Android + web/PWA icons from an existing image; the favicon generator covers only the web slice; splash-screens are launch images, not icons. Tests platform-coverage reasoning, not the word 'icon'.

dev.query: grade the condition and centering of my vintage Charizard card from a photo, PSA-style
dev.note: Single distinctive service: AI trading-card grading with corner/edge/centering analysis and PSA/Beckett-calibrated subgrades. 'Charizard' implies a Pokemon card without naming the card game; nothing else in the corpus grades collectibles.

dev.query: convert a .mov clip into an mp4 with H.264 so it plays on any device
dev.note: Distinctive video/audio re-encoder (container/codec change, H.264/AAC). The image-conversion services are near-neighbors by wording ('convert') but cannot touch video, so they are correctly excluded — a classic false-friend trap.

dev.query: has a specific GDPR provision been amended, or is the consolidated text I'm citing still current
dev.note: GDPR is an EU act, so the EUR-Lex act checker is the direct fit; the history timeline shows when it changed (strong partial); the French-code checker is the wrong corpus. Mirror-image of the French-law query to test jurisdiction routing.

dev.query: what does a contract ICU nurse typically earn in Texas right now
dev.note: The travel-nurse bill-rate benchmark by specialty/state is exactly a per-state ICU rate; the agency-markup analysis is adjacent (what the agency adds) rather than the take-home rate. Distinguishes pay rate from agency margin.

dev.query: pull together current openings for a marketing manager from the major job boards so I can apply
dev.note: The multi-board jobs scraper and the LinkedIn job search directly return apply-able listings; the general LinkedIn tool and the CoreSignal preview (no descriptions/URLs, step 1 only) are partials. Tests 'job boards to apply' vs enrichment/preview.

dev.query: flag whether a website's domain was set up only days ago, to catch a likely phishing site
dev.note: The domain-age checker is purpose-built for spotting brand-new suspicious domains; a WHOIS/RDAP lookup carries the creation date but leaves the age math to the caller. Query leads with the phishing motive, not 'domain age'.

dev.query: I have a shortlist of brand names — tell me which ones are still free to register
dev.note: Both check registration availability for a batch of names; the bulk checker adds multi-TLD scanning, so both are strong. The trap is age/WHOIS lookups that report on already-registered domains, which do not answer 'still free'.

dev.query: is the address hammering my server a known source of spam or malicious traffic
dev.note: DNSBL blacklist and AbuseIPDB reputation checks directly answer 'is this a bad IP'; the composite risk score and the IP profile (with a reputation field) are broader partials. Plain IP-geolocation endpoints are a tempting but wrong neighbor and are excluded.

dev.query: decode a car's 17-character chassis identifier into its make, model and year
dev.note: Two full NHTSA VIN decoders return make/model/year; the WMI decoder only reads the first three characters (manufacturer) and cannot give the model or year — a weak partial. '17-character chassis identifier' avoids the token 'VIN'.

dev.query: tell me if a given phone number is a mobile, a landline, or an internet line, and which country it belongs to
dev.note: Two validators explicitly return line type (mobile/landline/VOIP) plus country; the other two validate and give country/E.164 but are lighter on line-type detail. SMS-number-rental services in the corpus are a different need and excluded.

dev.query: I need to move money and want the least fees — compare what a transaction costs across the major EVM chains so I can route to the cheapest one
dev.note: Cross-chain fee comparison: evm-gas spans 17 chains (best), 402rates literally sorts a USDC transfer cheapest-first, agentexchange covers 6 chains, vibesprings only 4. Many near-identical gas oracles exist, so ranking must reward breadth.

dev.query: test whether a contract call would revert before I actually broadcast it and burn the fee
dev.note: 'Would it revert' is exactly the simulate endpoint (best); onesource's read-only eth_call also dry-runs a call but is framed as a generic read, not a revert check. Neither says 'dry-run' the way the query implies.

dev.query: before I release USDC to a counterparty, confirm their crypto wallet isn't on a government blocked-persons list
dev.note: OFAC wallet screening: wallet-screen adds mixer exposure + a signed receipt (best), eagle adds the Circle blacklist, sanctions-screen does address-or-name; induction only matches an entity NAME, not a wallet, so it's the weak one.

dev.query: the address I pasted looks almost identical to the one I copied — make sure it isn't a decoy trying to intercept my payment
dev.note: 'Almost identical decoy' is the address-poisoning look-alike check (best); recipient-check covers look-alikes plus known-malicious; address-reputation is a broader go/no-go verdict. Query avoids the term 'poisoning' entirely.

dev.query: I'm drawing a giveaway winner and need a random pick the entrants can independently prove wasn't rigged
dev.note: The hook is provable fairness, not just randomness: anchor/roll signs each draw (best), shizu offers commit-reveal receipts, drand-dice carries a proof transcript; agent402 is cryptographically secure but unverifiable, so it's the trap partial.

dev.query: produce a stable fingerprint of a chunk of text so I can later tell if even one character changed
dev.note: Integrity fingerprint: hash-hmac offers many algorithms plus timing-safe verify (best), agent402 the common SHA/MD5 set; webtools402 is Ethereum-flavoured (keccak/selector/namehash) so it's a weaker general-purpose fit.

dev.query: peek at the claims and expiry buried inside a login bearer token without checking whether the signature is valid
dev.note: A JWT is base64 under the hood so base64-decode partially works, but only jwt-decode parses claims/exp/alg directly and explicitly skips signature verification. Query never says 'JWT'.

dev.query: someone linked me a site I've never heard of — how recently was it set up, so I can judge whether it's a throwaway scam
dev.note: Domain-age-as-trust-signal: netintel adds Wayback history + an explicit fraud/phishing framing (best); ottoai and underscoredone both return creation date + age but with less scam-detection framing.

dev.query: I've settled on a brand name for my project — can I still grab the matching web address
dev.note: Registration-availability check: the underscoredone checker is single-purpose (best), netintel sweeps popular TLDs, ipintel returns an availability verdict. Query says 'grab the web address', sharing almost no tokens with 'domain registration'.

dev.query: an unfamiliar server keeps hitting us — has its address turned up on abuse or spam blocklists? I don't care where it is, just its reputation
dev.note: 'I don't care where it is' deliberately steers off geolocation: ip-blacklist checks 15 spam/abuse DNSBLs (best), ip-reputation adds threat feeds, ipintel does reputation but is geolocation-heavy so it's the weakest against this phrasing.

dev.query: current wholesale price levels for crude and the natural-gas benchmark, for an inflation read
dev.note: Energy price levels: crownblock is oil-and-gas specific (WTI/Brent/Henry Hub, best), eia-energy gives WTI + natural-gas spot, commodity-benchmark bundles energy with metals and grains so it's broader than asked.

dev.query: how much did leveraged crypto positions get wiped out in the past day, and was it mostly longs or shorts
dev.note: 24h forced-liquidation totals with long/short split; ochinimus reports exactly that, lonestar's full report is close, hyperextend is a raw single-asset tape you would have to aggregate yourself.

dev.query: what minimum price per kilo is a cocoa grower in Ivory Coast guaranteed by the marketing board
dev.note: Ivorian cocoa farmgate floor; lagoon's cocoa endpoint is the decreed floor, lonestar's ag report may cover it, stratalize's benchmark lists other crops but not cocoa.

dev.query: I want to time my compute for when the electricity behind it is least carbon-heavy, so what's the greenest window today
dev.note: hourly grid carbon intensity to time a workload; gridpulse gives the cleanest slot and forward curve, the grid report only shows the generation mix.

dev.query: convert a recipe's eight fluid ounces to milliliters and a couple of pounds to kilograms
dev.note: physical unit conversion across volume and mass; 2s.io's unit converter handles floz-to-ml and lb-to-kg directly.

dev.query: the bank account number I scanned off a paper invoice has a few illegible digits, so rebuild the correct one
dev.note: reconstructing a garbled account number from OCR; repair recovers unreadable characters and fixes check digits, resolve only validates and looks up an already-clean IBAN.

dev.query: before wiring funds, make sure the payee's bank isn't on any sanctions or watchlist
dev.note: sanctions screening of a payee bank; screen/batch checks the bank's BIC against OFAC/EU/UN lists, osf screens named parties generally, resolve only identifies the bank.

dev.query: turn my structured order details into a polished, multi-page invoice document to send a client
dev.note: PDF from structured data with an invoice template; generate-pdf renders JSON into a templated invoice, makespdf only converts hand-written markdown.

dev.query: spot the same real-world question priced differently on two betting exchanges so I can lock a riskless edge
dev.note: matched cross-venue event arbitrage; arb-cross and polynews both compare the same event across Polymarket and Kalshi, arb-basket is a single-market NO-basket strategy instead.

dev.query: warn me the moment a big dollar-pegged coin starts drifting below one dollar
dev.note: depeg alerting; stablecoin-watch emits downside depeg alerts on peg deviation, lonestar's pulse scores peg deviation and risk, apitoll only reports current peg price.

dev.query: draw a raffle winner from a list of entrants with a proof no one could have rigged it
dev.note: provably-fair selection from a list; pick chooses an entrant with a drand proof, shuffle only permutes the list, anchor's roll returns signed integers you would map yourself.

dev.query: just hand me a secure random integer between 1 and 100, nothing fancy
dev.note: plain secure random integer in a range; agent402 documents a min/max integer, rng.sociologic returns an integer in a range, anchor's roll adds treasury-signed verifiability that isn't needed here.

dev.query: buy a prepaid data plan for a phone I'll use traveling in Japan, paying with stablecoin
dev.note: prepaid travel data paid in crypto; esims/search finds the data plan, invoice/create prices and locks it, gift-cards/search is the wrong product line.

dev.query: when will the space station next pass over my location and where is it right now
dev.note: satellite pass prediction and live position; bip-rep tracks ISS position and predicts the next overhead pass for an observer.

dev.query: my model returned JSON with trailing commas and code fences that won't parse, so fix it so it loads
dev.note: fixing malformed JSON that won't parse; fenixfoundry repairs trailing commas and code fences, json-suite includes a fixer among many tools, the validator only reports errors without repairing.

dev.query: read a messy paragraph of contact info and return just name, email and price as fixed keys
dev.note: free-text to fixed keys; 402's ai-extract names the exact fields wanted, netintel maps arbitrary text to a supplied schema, agentx402 extracts from a URL rather than a raw text block.

dev.query: how crowded is the SOL perpetual right now, with open interest, skew and utilization in one snapshot
dev.note: single-market perp positioning snapshot; perps-market-structure gives current OI/skew/utilization for the Jupiter SOL market, payperbyte is cross-venue OI/funding, apitoll is generic per-coin perp data.

dev.query: is it cheaper to rent or to buy a home in this metro, using price indices and price-to-rent ratios
dev.note: rent-vs-buy housing metrics; residential-market returns price-to-rent and home-price indices, mortgage-market adds rate and affordability context, housing-supply is only starts and permits.

dev.query: will Brazilian electricity prices spike because the hydro reservoirs are running low
dev.note: hydro-driven power-price risk; cadeias/energia_br chains rainfall to reservoir levels to thermal-dispatch cost pressure, hidrologia gives the raw stored-hydro levels behind it.

locked.query: the call is at nine in the morning in Berlin, when is that for someone in Tokyo
locked.note: Sibling discrimination against the coordinate-to-zone lookups above: converting BETWEEN two zones is a different capability from resolving one. The wall-clock endpoint is partial (tells you the time in one zone, not the conversion).

locked.query: which airfields could a small plane reach within a hundred kilometres of here
locked.note: Two genuine alternatives, one public-records and one commercial-aviation. Competes against a large cluster of airport arrival/delay endpoints that are about a NAMED airport, not proximity search.

locked.query: how long can someone sit outside at midday before their skin burns
locked.note: The best answer literally computes burn times. The solar endpoint carries a uv-index tag but is really about sunrise/sunset and irradiance, so it is only partially relevant. Hard: dozens of weather endpoints share this vocabulary.

locked.query: my hay fever is flaring up, how bad is it outside today
locked.note: Zero vocabulary overlap — the resource says 'pollen allergen index counts (grass, birch, oak)' and the query says none of that. Pure paraphrase test against a very crowded weather cluster.

locked.query: could a solar storm degrade GPS accuracy in the next hour
locked.note: Two equally-good planetary K-index feeds from different providers. Must beat the general 'space' AI-reasoning endpoints, which answer astronomy questions rather than serving the index.

locked.query: is the river near this town about to overflow its banks
locked.note: A forecast service and a warnings scanner are both right answers; the raw gauge-height feed is the input to both, so it is secondary.

locked.query: are there fires burning close to this location right now
locked.note: Sibling discrimination by scope: the Brazil-only hotspot feed and the global multi-hazard disaster feed both technically contain fires but neither answers 'near this location' generally.

locked.query: are planes being held on the ground at American airports today
locked.note: Ground stops and ATC delays. Competes with the arrivals board and the airspace tracker from the same publisher, which share the transit/airport tags but answer different questions.

locked.query: what has just landed at this airport
locked.note: Sibling pair with the FAA-delays entry above; both are 'airport status' but only one is an arrivals list.

locked.query: are the trains running to schedule in Europe
locked.note: Must not be won by the subway-alerts sibling, which is a single metro system rather than European rail.

locked.query: how long has this website been around
locked.note: Cross-vendor sibling pair. Hard because both vendors also publish WHOIS/registration endpoints that return the creation date as one field among many.

locked.query: find near-miss spellings of our brand that a phisher could register
locked.note: Distinctive capability, but the corpus has a large brand-protection and phishing cluster to beat.

locked.query: has this password already leaked somewhere
locked.note: Easy anchor query — if a lexical ranker misses this one something is structurally wrong.

locked.query: what stack is this site built on
locked.note: Application stack versus hosting infrastructure — a real, fine distinction between two same-vendor siblings sharing the word 'fingerprint'.

locked.query: how many usable hosts fit in a slash twenty-six
locked.note: Spelled-out CIDR prefix so the query shares almost no tokens with the description.

locked.query: am I allowed to fetch pages from this site automatically
locked.note: Crawl permission. The agent-accessibility report checks the same signals as part of a wider audit; the Minifetch preflight only answers it for Minifetch's own crawler, so it is grade 1. Hard because the corpus is full of scrapers that ignore the question entirely.

locked.query: what did this page look like a few years ago
locked.note: Web archive lookup. The query says nothing about archives, Wayback or the Internet Archive.

locked.query: has this address been reported for attacks or abuse
locked.note: Deliberately ambiguous 'address': the corpus is full of BLOCKCHAIN address-risk scoring that shares almost every word. A ranker that returns wallet screening here has misread the domain.

locked.query: which services are listening on this machine
locked.note: Neither 'port' nor 'scan' is in the query.

locked.query: make scannable squares for a batch of links I want to print
locked.note: Pure paraphrase — the query avoids 'QR' entirely and describes the artefact.

locked.query: prove a file has not been altered since I last saw it
locked.note: Two vendors, same primitive. The query never says hash, checksum or digest.

locked.query: run this python snippet somewhere isolated and show me the output
locked.note: Only sandboxed-execution service in this slice of the corpus; a good check that a rare capability is reachable at all.

locked.query: how much of my context window will this passage use
locked.note: The resource mentions an 'LLM token estimate' once, at the end of a list of counts. Everything else in the query is unshared vocabulary.

locked.query: pick a winner fairly and let me prove afterwards the draw was not rigged
locked.note: Selection specifically, from a family of verifiable-randomness siblings. The plain CSPRNG endpoint is relevant but cannot prove anything after the fact, so grade 1.

locked.query: how many kilograms is twelve stone
locked.note: Sole unit converter in the corpus, but it must beat a very large currency-conversion cluster that owns the word 'convert'.

locked.query: check a shipping container number is well formed before filing the paperwork
locked.note: ISO 6346 check-digit validation. Paired with the next two judgments to test format-validation versus data-lookup.

locked.query: verify a product barcode number is valid without looking anything up
locked.note: Offline check-digit validation. Its sibling resolves the barcode to product metadata, which is a different job — the 'without looking anything up' clause is the whole discrimination.

locked.query: what will the monthly repayment be on a thirty year home loan
locked.note: Competes with a large mortgage-RATE reporting cluster; only this one computes a schedule.

locked.query: what would a 1990 salary be worth in today's money
locked.note: Must beat the many CPI and inflation-benchmark feeds, which report the index rather than adjusting an amount.

locked.query: did anyone on the board sell their own company's stock recently
locked.note: Deliberate near-miss with the congressional-trading pair above: both are 'politically interesting people trading stock', only one is SEC Form 4.

locked.query: was trading in this ticker paused today
locked.note: Rare capability inside an enormous equities cluster.

locked.query: when does this company next pay out to shareholders
locked.note: Templated route. Tests that a path-parameter resource is still findable from natural language.

locked.query: read this text aloud and give me back an audio file
locked.note: A genuinely crowded capability — seven providers, three tiers from one of them. Any of the top three is a correct first result; the tiered variants are the same service at another price point.

locked.query: make a scanned document searchable without changing how it looks
locked.note: Three same-vendor siblings in strict order: invisible text layer, extracted text, and plain text extraction from a born-digital PDF. 'Without changing how it looks' is the only clue separating the first two.

locked.query: turn document pages into pictures so I can show a preview strip
locked.note: The storyboard sibling also produces a preview strip, but from video frames — a plausible wrong answer that shares the intent words and not the input type.

locked.query: cut a thirty second segment out of a recording without losing quality

locked.query: obscure faces and number plates before I publish the picture

locked.query: which language is this text written in

locked.query: has this employer been cited for workplace safety breaches

locked.query: the standard global identifier for a legal entity in financial filings

locked.query: who are the directors behind a French company

locked.query: which days are non-working in this country next year

locked.query: what date is ten working days from now if I skip public holidays

locked.query: confirm a diagnosis code a clinician wrote down is a real one

locked.query: has this medicine been pulled from shelves for safety reasons

locked.query: book me a table for dinner tonight

locked.query: is this npm package actively maintained and widely used

locked.query: find an accepted answer for a programming error someone else hit
locked.note: Must beat the general web-search cluster, which is enormous and also answers questions.

locked.query: get the captions from a video so I can quote it
locked.note: Fetching an existing caption track, not speech-to-text — the deliberate mirror of the transcription judgment above.

locked.query: list the accounts following this person on X

locked.query: turn a syndication feed into structured JSON

locked.query: an original story to read a child at bedtime

locked.query: which flowers does a particular kind of honey come from

locked.query: what price do West African growers actually receive for their beans

locked.query: find shops and restaurants near a given place
locked.note: Local business search. Must beat the general web-search cluster, which is one of the largest families in the corpus.

locked.query: find a guaranteed no-loss edge where the same real-world event is priced differently on two betting exchanges

locked.query: spend my frequent-flyer miles on a lie-flat business seat and see which dates actually have availability

locked.query: are planes being held on the ground at Chicago O'Hare because of the storm

locked.query: I have a snippet of text and only need to know what language it is written in, not a translation

locked.query: a scanned invoice gave me a bank account number with a couple of characters unreadable — reconstruct the correct one
locked.note: The repair endpoint specifically recomputes check digits and recovers unreadable characters from OCR; resolve only validates a clean number. Query never says 'IBAN', only 'bank account number' and 'scanned/unreadable'.

locked.query: verify a European bank account number's check digits are correct before I wire money to it
locked.note: Two deterministic IBAN mod-97 validators are the direct answer; resolve validates too but does more; the BIC checker validates the wrong identifier (bank code, not account). Tests IBAN-vs-BIC discrimination.

locked.query: make sure the identifier stamped on an intermodal shipping box isn't a transcription typo before the bill of lading is filed
locked.note: Uniquely the ISO 6346 container-number check-digit validator, aimed at catching errors before a B/L. 'Intermodal shipping box' + 'bill of lading' describe the need without saying 'container number' or 'ISO 6346'.

locked.query: one of my product barcodes keeps getting rejected by the marketplace — check whether the number itself is corrupted
locked.note: The GTIN/EAN/UPC checksum validator explicitly targets barcodes Amazon/Google reject. Query uses 'barcode/corrupted/rejected' rather than the term 'GTIN', testing the synonym mapping.

locked.query: confirm a business is registered to clear goods through customs in the European Union
locked.note: The EORI validator is exactly 'the number every business needs to clear customs in the EU'. The query deliberately spells out the customs-clearance need instead of the acronym EORI.

locked.query: is this clause of the French labour code still valid law today or has it been struck out

locked.query: screen a new customer's name against government watchlists to see if they're subject to sanctions

locked.query: has a particular brand of blood-pressure medication been pulled from shelves for a safety problem

locked.query: what pay did tech companies officially report to the government for their visa-sponsored foreign workers
locked.note: Uniquely the H-1B prevailing-wage dataset from DOL LCA filings, by employer. The query describes visa-sponsored wage disclosures without the token 'H-1B'.

locked.query: before I add a lead to my list, tell me whether their email address is fake, a throwaway, or won't accept mail

locked.query: how long is the wait for a table at a busy restaurant right now

locked.query: roughly how backed up is the Bitcoin network right now, and what fee would get a payment confirmed

locked.query: how hard is it at the moment to mine a fresh Bitcoin block
locked.note: 'How hard to mine' = proof-of-work difficulty (getdifficulty, best); getmininginfo bundles difficulty with hashrate; getnetworkhashps is only a hashrate proxy. Sibling RPCs on one host that a lexical match can't separate.

locked.query: give me a full readout of what one address holds on Base — its native coin plus every token sitting in it
locked.note: 'Coin plus every token' — orcpin returns native + ERC-20 holdings and flags (best), statepulse scans native + ERC-20, but agentexchange returns only the native balance and nonce so it misses the tokens the query asks for.

locked.query: I have a transaction hash and want a plain-language explanation of what it actually moved and called

locked.query: an app is asking my wallet to sign something — break down which token, spender and cap I'd be approving before I click

locked.query: my app displays raw 0x wallet strings and I want to show a friendly readable name for each one instead
locked.note: Address-to-name (reverse) lookup: justaname's reverse endpoint is purpose-built (best), agentexchange and ens-resolver are bidirectional so they cover it too, zapper returns social identities (ENS/Farcaster/Lens) as a weaker fit.

locked.query: which machines actually accept incoming mail for a particular domain

locked.query: remind me how many days are left before a website's security certificate lapses

locked.query: pull up the yearly report a public company is required to file with the securities regulator
